subject: E-Commerce
title: Warehouse Robots Take Over
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Warehouse Robots Take Over.

hook.text: Amazon bought Kiva Systems for $775 million in 2012. Now 750,000 robots work alongside humans in its warehouses.

buildup.text: Kiva robots are orange disc-shaped units that slide under shelving pods and carry them to picking stations.

discovery.text: Robots reduced the cost of picking and packing by 20-40%. They work 24/7, don't need breaks, and never get lost.

twist.text: Robots haven't replaced humans yet. Picking individual items from a mixed shelf still requires human hands.

climax.text: The warehouse of the future is dark—no lights needed when robots work alone. It's called a 'dark warehouse.'

punchline.text: 750,000 robots, 20-40% cheaper. But human hands still pick what robots can't.

quiz.question: Why hasn't automation fully replaced humans in warehouses?
options: Picking individual mixed items still requires human dexterity
